standard_prerequisites.name: Restriction of the big etale site to a small one
standard_prerequisites.statement: For f : U -> X in the big etale site one has i_f o pi_X = f as morphisms of ringed sites U_etale -> X_etale, and restriction along i_f is exact.
standard_prerequisites.use: It identifies H_etale|_{U_etale} with the degree-one homology of f^*F_bullet at source lines 1650-1658.

standard_prerequisites.name: The quasi-coherent review lemma
standard_prerequisites.statement: The presheaf Y -> Gamma(Y, f^*F) satisfies the fpqc (hence fppf and etale) sheaf condition (the author's lemma-review-quasi-coherent, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It gives that H_etale is an fppf sheaf and hence H_etale = epsilon_{X,*}H_fppf at source lines 1672-1682.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cech vanishing criterion for a collection of coverings
standard_prerequisites.statement: If Cech cohomology vanishes for a suitable collection of coverings, then the sheaf cohomology vanishes (Cohomology on Sites, declared as a tagged source pointer).
standard_prerequisites.use: It reduces the vanishing to the displayed Cech comparison at source lines 1685-1691.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cech vanishing for quasi-coherent modules on a standard covering
standard_prerequisites.statement: The standard covering Cech complex of a quasi-coherent module has no higher cohomology (Descent, declared as a tagged source pointer).
standard_prerequisites.use: It finishes the proof at source lines 1700-1702.

core_obligations: Local computation: identify H_etale|_{U_etale} with the degree-one homology of f^*F_bullet, note it is quasi-coherent, and prove compatibility with flat base change (source lines 1650-1669).

Sheaf property: for an fppf covering with affine pieces, use the quasi-coherent review lemma to show the sheaf condition holds, so H_etale is already an fppf sheaf and H_etale = epsilon_{X,*}H_fppf (source lines 1672-1682).

Vanishing: apply the Cech vanishing criterion to the collection of affine objects and finite fppf coverings, rewrite the Cech complex using the values computed in the first paragraph, and invoke Cech vanishing for quasi-coherent modules (source lines 1684-1702).

proof_roadmap.step: Compute the restriction of H_etale to U_etale as the degree-one homology of f^*F_bullet and check flat base change.
Use the quasi-coherent review lemma to get the fppf sheaf property and the identity H_etale = epsilon_{X,*}H_fppf.
Prove the vanishing by the Cech criterion, the identification of Cech complexes, and Cech vanishing for quasi-coherent modules.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-vanishing-adequate at source lines 1615-1639: for a complex F_1 -> F_2 -> F_3 of quasi-coherent O_X-modules, the homology sheaf H_etale on the big etale site (built from the pi_X^*-pullbacks) equals epsilon_{X,*}H_fppf for the corresponding fppf homology sheaf, and both H^p_etale(U, H_etale) and H^p_fppf(U, H_fppf) vanish for p > 0 at every affine object U. The author's proof at source lines 1649-1703 first studies the restriction of H_etale to U_etale, identifies it with the degree-one homology of the complex f^*F_bullet using i_f o pi_X = f, observes that it is quasi-coherent, and shows compatibility with flat base change g : V -> U; then deduces the fppf sheaf property for H_etale from part (1) of the chapter's quasi-coherent review lemma (retained as context), which identifies H_fppf with H_etale; and finally proves the vanishing by applying the Cech vanishing criterion for the collection of affine objects with finite fppf coverings (a cross-chapter pointer), rewriting the Cech complex using the first paragraph, and concluding by Cech vanishing for quasi-coherent modules on a standard covering (a second pointer). The counted argument is therefore a complete three-part proof whose in-chapter ingredient is available inside the package.
